headline: Graph and contrastive learning predict drug, RNA and gene-regulatory associations
label: Graph Learning For Association Prediction
summary: Recent papers pair graph networks and language-model embeddings with contrastive and multimodal learning to predict biological associations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is learning representations over biological graphs or multimodal inputs and applying them to association prediction. Graph architectures recur across drug-drug interaction (RGCN and HGT benchmarks), drug-target prediction (BioHSNet, LI-DTI), miRNA-disease and circRNA-miRNA association (MRGBMDAT, HMA-GCA, SSMVCL), and gene regulatory network inference (scHyperLink, MultiCausGRN). Language-model embeddings serve as node or sequence features, including BioBERT over Gene Ontology annotations for synthetic lethality, BERT embeddings for dark kinases, and RNA-FM and ChemBERTa for circRNA-drug associations. Contrastive objectives form a second strategy, aligning drug structures with Cell Painting morphology, L1000 perturbation transcriptomics, and SELFIES-based molecular representations with knowledge-graph context. The newer elements are the pairing of these learned representations with interpretability or leakage-aware evaluation, as in LI-DTI, the explainable HGT framework, and the knowledge graph embedding leakage benchmark.
